title: ConvexFiniteSumMeanSquareHessian.lean

problem_class.label: convex
problem_class.details: The objective is convex on all of ℝᵈ. Individual components may be nonconvex.
problem_class.evidence: LongTails/Setups/ConvexFiniteSumMeanSquareHessian.lean, spec.admissible requires ConvexOn ℝ Set.univ (objective I).

problem_class.label: finite_sum
problem_class.details: The objective is the equally weighted mean F(x) = (1/n)∑ᵢ fᵢ(x) of n twice continuously differentiable components.

oracle.label: component_gradient
oracle.details: The gradient is the exact gradient of the selected component. The reply is independent of oracle seed and query history.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/ConvexFiniteSumMeanSquareHessian.lean, spec.admissible specifies O.answer for every history, seed, i, and x.

oracle.label: function_value
oracle.details: A single query at an algorithm-chosen index i and point x returns fᵢ(x), ∇fᵢ(x), and ∇²fᵢ(x) together.

oracle.label: other
oracle.details: The second-order part of the reply is the full exact component Hessian as a linear operator on ℝᵈ.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/ConvexFiniteSumMeanSquareHessian.lean, Reply and the fderiv ℝ (gradient (I.f i)) x field of the answer in spec.admissible.

distinctive_assumptions.label: generalized_smoothness
distinctive_assumptions.details: For every x,y, (1/n)∑ᵢ ‖∇²fᵢ(x)−∇²fᵢ(y)‖op² ≤ H²‖x−y‖₂². The square is taken before averaging over components.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/ConvexFiniteSumMeanSquareHessian.lean, Reply and the summed squared-norm inequality in spec.admissible.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: The domain is Euclidean ℝᵈ with d ≥ 2¹⁷⁰ n³(1+K)¹², where K = ⌈(HR³/(√n ε))^(2/7)⌉.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: The algorithm knows n, d, H, R, and ε, with n ≥ 1, H ≥ 0, R > 0, and ε > 0. The component functions and a global minimizer x⋆ with ‖x⋆‖₂ ≤ R belong to the hidden instance. Algorithms may use private randomness and choose queries adaptively, without a span restriction.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/ConvexFiniteSumMeanSquareHessian.lean, Params, Instance, spec.publicInput, spec.valid, and spec.admissible. LongTails/Template.lean, Algorithm and Setup.allowedAlgorithm.

accuracy.label: objective_gap
accuracy.details: The returned point X must be measurable, its objective gap must be integrable, and E[F(X)−F(x⋆)] ≤ ε.

accuracy.label: expected
accuracy.details: The guarantee averages the output gap over the execution law. With exact replies at every query, algorithm randomization can still affect the output.
accuracy.evidence: LongTails/Setups/ConvexFiniteSumMeanSquareHessian.lean, spec.successful and spec.admissible. LongTails/Template.lean, Algorithm.law and Convergence.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: The setup combines convexity of the average with mean-square Lipschitz continuity of component Hessians, access to a full Hessian at any chosen component, and a dimension threshold tied to accuracy.

descriptionHtml:
Second-Order Convex Finite-Sum Minimization

We minimize a convex function F on Rd, the average of n twice continuously differentiable components. Their Hessians are Lipschitz in root mean square with constant H≥0, and a global minimizer x⋆ satisfies ∥x⋆∥≤R for a radius R>0. The oracle returns the value, gradient, and Hessian of a chosen component at a queried point. For a tolerance ε>0, the goal is a measurable output x¯∈Rd with integrable objective gap satisfying E[F(x¯)−F(x⋆)]≤ε, where the expectation is over the algorithm’s randomness.

Writing fi:Rd→R for component i, define F(x)=1n∑i=1nfi(x). The optimization problem is minx∈RdF(x). The algorithm receives n,d,H,R,ε. The component count n and dimension d are positive integers in the regime K=⌈(HR3nε)2/7⌉,d≥2170n3(1+K)12. We use the Euclidean norm ∥⋅∥ and its induced operator norm ∥⋅∥op.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Convexity and minimizer radius). For all x,y∈Rd and t∈[0,1], F((1−t)x+ty)≤(1−t)F(x)+tF(y). There exists x⋆∈Rd with ∥x⋆∥≤R such that F(x⋆)≤F(x) for every x∈Rd.

Assumption 2 (Mean-square Hessian regularity). Each fi is twice continuously differentiable. For all x,y∈Rd, 1n∑i=1n‖∇2fi(x)−∇2fi(y)‖op2≤H2∥x−y∥2.

A query specifies any i∈{1,…,n} and x∈Rd and returns the exact triple (fi(x),∇fi(x),∇2fi(x)). After the allotted oracle calls, the output x¯ must be measurable, its objective gap must be integrable, and it must satisfy E[F(x¯)−F(x⋆)]≤ε.

theorems.referencesHtml: • Artem Tsedenov and Dmitry Kovalev. An Optimal Second-Order Algorithm for Finite-Sum Optimization under Average Smoothness and Convexity. 2026 (arXiv v1). Complexity: Ω(n+n6/7(HR3/ε)2/7) component second-order oracle calls in expectation for stochastic second-order span methods initialized at zero with independently and uniformly sampled indices, for H,R,ε>0.
theorems.formulaHtml: ⌊n⋅(1+(H⋅R3n⋅ε)27)216⌋+

comparisonHtml:
On Rd, F=n−1∑ifi is convex, each fi is C2, and n−1∑i∥∇2fi(x)−∇2fi(y)∥2≤H2∥x−y∥2 for all x,y. Some minimizer x⋆ satisfies ∥x⋆∥≤R. Take n≥1, H≥0, R,ε>0, and d≥2170n3(1+⌈(S/n)2/7⌉)12. A query (i,x) returns the exact value, gradient, and full Hessian of fi at x. The target is ∫(F(x^(ω))−F(x⋆))dP(ω)≤ε for a measurable output with integrable gap under the run law P.

Necessary component-oracle budgets for convex finite sums with mean-square Lipschitz Hessians
Result Oracle complexity Novelty Limitations
(1) ConvexFiniteSumMeanSquareHessianLowerBound (Ours) (⋆⋆⋆) (review) Necessary budget Ω(n+n6/7S2/7) component calls under a fixed cap
(2) (Tsedenov and Kovalev 2026), Thm. 2 Necessary budget Ω(n+n6/7S2/7) expected component calls (1): Matches the order and removes the linear-span and IID uniform-index restrictions. Allows adaptive indices, arbitrary probes, and unrestricted full-Hessian use. (1): Fixed caps versus expected work. Requires much higher dimension than d≍(S/n)2/7 for the accuracy term when S exceeds a universal multiple of n.
(3) (Zhang et al. 2026), Thm. 4.1. Convex components with individually H-Lipschitz Hessians. Necessary budget Ω(n+n5/7S2/7) component calls, including full batches (1): Covers adaptive indices and arbitrary probes beyond periodic full batches, uniform sampling, and zero-respecting queries. The larger accuracy term applies to the broader mean-square class. (1): The lower bound does not extend to individually Lipschitz Hessians. Expected gap versus failure with probability 13/16 for the accuracy term (H>0, at least n iterations).

Abbr: S=HR3/ε. Hessian norms are operator norms.

Tsedenov, Artem, and Dmitry Kovalev. 2026. An Optimal Second-Order Algorithm for Finite-Sum Optimization Under Average Smoothness and Convexity. https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2610.10495.
Zhang, Xinliang, Lesi Chen, Zonghan Li, and Jingzhao Zhang. 2026. Near-Optimal Second-Order Convex Finite-Sum Optimization Under Individual Smoothness. https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2610.42040.

import LongTails.Template
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Gradient.Basic
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.ContDiff.Defs
import Mathlib.Analysis.Convex.Function
import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Lp.MeasurableSpace
import Mathlib.Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Pow.Real
import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Integral.Bochner.Basic

namespace LongTails.Setups.ConvexFiniteSumMeanSquareHessian

open OracleTemplate MeasureTheory

structure Params where
  n : ℕ
  d : ℕ
  H : ℝ
  R : ℝ
  ε : ℝ

abbrev Point (p : Params) := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p.d)
abbrev Reply (p : Params) := ℝ × Point p × (Point p →L[ℝ] Point p)

structure Instance (p : Params) where
  f : Fin p.n → Point p → ℝ
  xstar : Point p

noncomputable def objective {p : Params} (I : Instance p) (x : Point p) : ℝ :=
  (∑ i, I.f i x) / p.n

noncomputable abbrev spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Params
  publicInput p := p
  Instance := Instance
  Query p := Fin p.n × Point p
  Reply := Reply
  Output := Point
  valid p :=
    let K := ⌈(p.H * p.R ^ 3 / (Real.sqrt p.n * p.ε)) ^ (2 / 7 : ℝ)⌉₊
    0 < p.n ∧ 0 ≤ p.H ∧ 0 < p.R ∧ 0 < p.ε ∧ 2 ^ 170 * p.n ^ 3 * (1 + K) ^ 12 ≤ p.d
  admissible p I O :=
    (∀ i, ContDiff ℝ 2 (I.f i)) ∧ ConvexOn ℝ Set.univ (objective I) ∧
    (∀ x y, ∑ i, ‖fderiv ℝ (gradient (I.f i)) x - fderiv ℝ (gradient (I.f i)) y‖ ^ 2 ≤
      p.n * p.H ^ 2 * ‖x - y‖ ^ 2) ∧
    ‖I.xstar‖ ≤ p.R ∧ (∀ x, objective I I.xstar ≤ objective I x) ∧
    (∀ history seed i x, O.answer history (0, i, x) seed =
      (I.f i x, gradient (I.f i) x, fderiv ℝ (gradient (I.f i)) x))
  successful p I output P :=
    Measurable output ∧ Integrable (fun ω => objective I (output ω) - objective I I.xstar) (P : Measure _) ∧
      (∫ ω, objective I (output ω) - objective I I.xstar ∂(P : Measure _)) ≤ p.ε

end LongTails.Setups.ConvexFiniteSumMeanSquareHessian
